title: EdgeFile X7: the route from access to apex
topic: The manufacturer's EdgeFile X7 shaping sequence and settings as a metro map, with per-file habits and one in vitro evidence flag.

claims.claim: Line info (header 'IFU · DFU'): speed 300–500 rpm; torque limit 300 g·cm
claims.source: Manufacturer directions, not evidence. EdgeEndo, Instructions for Use – EdgeFile X7, REF 99.EX7.10.01A.XX (undated; PDF created 5 Mar 2026), edgeendo.com, accessed 22 Nov 2026, section 1 ('Recommended speed 300-500 rpm continuous rotation. Torque limit: 300 g·cm (2.94 N·cm)'). EdgeEndo, Rotary/Reciprocating Files Directions for Use, DFU-RF-US Rev D 06/23, edgeendo.com, accessed 22 Nov 2026 offers the same values as an option ('Or if you wish, you can use ... Speed: 300-500 rpm, Torque: 2.94 N-cm/300 g-cm')

claims.claim: Route: ACCESS → SCOUT → WORKING LENGTH: #10 K, then #15 K (apex locator and radiograph pictograms) = glide path
claims.source: Manufacturer. IFU (REF 99.EX7.10.01A.XX) 'Simplified Technique Guide' steps 1, 2 and 4 ('#10 K file or larger ... with an apex locator and radiographs ... This will also form a glide path'); DFU-RF-US Rev D 06/23: 'Establish patency by taking a #10 K-File 1mm past the canal terminus, and at least a #15 K-File to the terminus.' The label satisfies both

claims.claim: Evidence · in vitro: hand preflaring first, shaped about 6× more blocks (ProTaper S1, resin blocks: mean 59 vs 10 before breaking)
claims.source: Berutti E, Negro AR, Lendini M, Pasqualini D. J Endod 2004;30(4):228-30 (PMID 15085052, doi:10.1097/00004770-200404000-00011); abstract only; conventional NiTi, not EdgeFile X7; the size of the manual preflaring is not given in the abstract

claims.claim: 17/.04, then 25/.04; 20/.04 only after the 25 stops short (alternate 20 and 25)
claims.source: Manufacturer: IFU (REF 99.EX7.10.01A.XX), 'Simplified Technique Guide' steps 5-6; this technique is printed in the IFU only, not in DFU-RF-US Rev D

claims.claim: Every file: irrigate · recap #10–15 · clean flutes · inspect
claims.source: Manufacturer directions (no literature cited): IFU step 3 (irrigate before each hand or rotary file) and section 5 (clean flutes, inspect, discard if distorted); 'recapitulate with a #10 or #15 tip hand file' is the crown-down wording in the IFU and in DFU-RF-US Rev D 06/23

claims.claim: If wanted: larger .04 (all canals) or larger .06 (straight to mildly curved); white dashed core = conditional service
claims.source: Manufacturer: IFU step 7 (larger .04 or .06 instruments if the clinician desires); the taper rule comes from the crown-down section headings (IFU; DFU-RF-US Rev D 06/23); no angle is given

Final irrigation: DFU-RF-US Rev D 06/23, 'Disinfecting' (after each canal is fully shaped: 17% EDTA 1 min, then 5% NaOCl 5 min, then further rinses); not a step of the IFU simplified technique. Recipe not shown. Cone fit: IFU and DFU-RF-US Rev D 06/23 ('may need to drop down in cone tip size'); Keith et al., J Endod 2024;50(12):1766-71 (PMID 39393517; abstract, EdgeTaper Platinum not X7)

claims.claim: One patient · one procedure · then discard; follow the current DFU
claims.source: Manufacturer: IFU section 5 ('up to four (4) canals during a single procedure. Discard after use'); DFU-RF-US Rev D 06/23 ('single use only'). The on-screen wording is true under both

claims.claim: Fine print: schematic · manufacturer IFU / US DFU + one in vitro study · no sequence is proven 'most efficient'
claims.source: No study comparing EdgeFile X7 sequences found on PubMed (searches of 22 Nov 2026, RESEARCH.md); Peters OA, J Endod 2004;30(8):559-67 (PMID 15273636; abstract) lists instrument sequence among the less significant factors

caption:
EdgeFile X7, access to apex, as a transit map.

Main line = the simplified technique in the IFU: #10 then #15 K to length; 17/.04, 25/.04; 20/.04 only if the 25 stops short. The US DFU (Rev D 06/23) prints crown-down only: check the leaflet in your box.
300–500 rpm, torque limit 300 g·cm.
Habits shown = manufacturer directions. Only the flag is literature: in vitro, ProTaper S1 in resin blocks, not X7. No study compares X7 sequences, so none is proven "most efficient".

Refs: EdgeEndo IFU EdgeFile X7 + DFU-RF-US Rev D, accessed Nov 2026; Berutti 2004, J Endod

caption_extras: The simplified technique is printed only in the multilingual IFU (REF 99.EX7.10.01A.XX, PDF dated Mar 2026). Crown-down 25 → 20 → (17) is in both documents and is the only X7 sequence in the US DFU (Rev D 06/23).
US DFU: #10 K 1 mm past the terminus for patency, at least #15 K to the terminus.
Berutti 2004 (J Endod): mean 59 vs 10 resin blocks shaped before S1 breakage; the preflaring size is not in the abstract.
Inspect: the IFU says discard at any distortion; the US DFU (Rev D) says heat-treated files may be used until they unwind backwards. The conservative rule is to discard.
Speed and torque limit as recommended in the IFU; the US DFU offers the same values as an option. "Minimal apical pressure" is US DFU wording.
IFU order shown. Re-confirm working length after coronal flaring (Stabholz 1995, J Endod; Ibarrola 1999, J Endod).
US DFU: take each file to length once, for no more than one second.
US DFU final rinse ('Disinfecting') is printed in the leaflet; the recipe is not shown in the reel.
